name: Cable Crossover
summary: A chest isolation exercise performed standing between dual cable pulleys, bringing the arms forward and across the body against constant tension.

setup: Attach single-grip handles to both high or mid-height pulleys of a dual-cable crossover station.
Grasp a handle in each hand, step forward into the center to place tension on the cables, and adopt a staggered stance.
Lean forward slightly from the hips with a tall chest, keeping a slight, fixed bend in your elbows.
steps: Sweep your hands forward and inward along a wide arc toward the midline of your body.
Bring your hands together or cross your wrists slightly at full contraction, squeezing the chest hard for a brief pause.
Slowly reverse the motion, opening your arms back out until you feel a deep stretch across your pectorals, maintaining the fixed elbow angle.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as your arms open into the stretched position; exhale forcefully as you bring your hands together.
cues: Squeeze the chest, not the hands

common_faults.fault: Turning the fly into a chest press by excessively bending and extending the elbows.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a consistent slight bend in your elbows throughout the entire range of motion.

common_faults.fault: Swinging the torso back and forth to generate momentum.
common_faults.correction: Brace the core, maintain a stable staggered stance, and keep the torso stationary.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the shoulders to shrug up toward the ears at the peak stretch.
common_faults.correction: Depress your scapulae and keep your shoulders down and back.

precautions: Do not allow the weights to pull your arms excessively behind the plane of the torso to avoid anterior shoulder capsule strain.
